name: Cho Hyun-sang
current_role: Vice Chairman & CEO, HS Hyosung (holding company spun off from Hyosung in July 2024)
profile: Youngest son of late Hyosung chairman Cho Suck-rae. Brown economics grad who started at Bain & Co. and joined Hyosung in 2000; after the 2024 split he leads HS Hyosung (advanced materials incl. tire cord, carbon fiber; pushing into AI, batteries and chip materials) while brother Cho Hyun-joon runs Hyosung.
interesting_fact: He chaired the APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) for 2025, presenting its report to APEC leaders at the Gyeongju summit; AI cooperation was a core agenda item.
deep_cut_fact: Between Bain and his Hyosung career he worked at Japan's NTT Communications, leading wired/wireless strategy projects and helping set up its Korean branch.
notes: Romanized also as Jo Hyun-sang / Hyun Sang Cho. In Dec 2025 HS Hyosung named Kim Kyoo-young as first non-family chairman; Cho remains vice chairman. Best route: HS Hyosung corporate communications.

name: Marcus Evans
current_role: Founder and owner, Marcus Evans Group (business conferences, summits, corporate hospitality)
profile: London-born entrepreneur (b. 1963) who founded what became the Marcus Evans Group in 1983; it runs thousands of B2B conferences, exhibitions and summits in ~32 countries, plus hospitality (THG Sports Tours) and training (Linguarama). Owned Ipswich Town FC from 2007 until selling to a US consortium in April 2021.
interesting_fact: His TV arm, Marcus Evans Entertainment, brought in World Productions (producer of Line of Duty) in 2012 before ITV Studios took a majority stake in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started out at about 20 with Associated Promotions (1983), selling corporate hospitality when it was a new market; it became The Hospitality Group / THG Sports Tours, still part of his group.
notes: Famously publicity-shy; rarely gives interviews and historically communicated via his executives. Best route is through Marcus Evans Group corporate channels. Relevant angle: his group runs energy/infrastructure business summits.

name: Yang Lijuan
current_role: Senior executive at Haidilao International Holding (since Apr 2026), leading its 'Red Pomegranate' multi-brand incubation plan; previously CEO of Super Hi International (Jul 2024-Apr 2026)
profile: Co-founding employee of hot-pot chain Haidilao who started as a teenage server in the 1990s and rose to COO, then group CEO (2022-24), where she led the 'Woodpecker Plan' turnaround. She ran overseas arm Super Hi (Nasdaq/HKEX) from 2024 and returned to Haidilao in April 2026 to drive new-brand growth. Holds ~3.7% of Haidilao.
interesting_fact: As Haidilao CEO she led the 'Woodpecker Plan' from late 2021, closing ~300 underperforming stores; the company swung back to profit in 2022 and earned about RMB 4.5bn net profit in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: She joined Haidilao before age 20 as a front-line server on 160 yuan a month, earning the nickname 'the most amazing server' and being promoted roughly every six months; she later led the chain's first overseas openings in Singapore and the US (2012-13).
notes: Also romanized Yang Lijuan / June Yang; some Chinese media write 杨丽娟. Li Yu succeeded her as Super Hi CEO in April 2026. Route via Haidilao media/IR.

name: Liu Jianguo
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Delijia Transmission Technology (Jiangsu) Co. (德力佳, SSE: 603092)
profile: Gearbox engineer (b. 1969, Shanghai Jiao Tong graduate) who spent ~20 years at Nanjing High Speed Gear / NGC, rising to chief engineer and GM. In 2017 he co-founded Delijia, which makes wind-turbine main gearboxes; it listed on the Shanghai main board in Nov 2025 and ranks among the top global suppliers, with Envision and Sany Renewable as key partners.
interesting_fact: Delijia went from founding (Jan 2017) to a Shanghai main-board IPO (Nov 7, 2025) in about eight years, becoming one of the world's top-three wind main-gearbox shippers by some broker estimates.
deep_cut_fact: When Delijia was set up in 2017 (with Sany Renewable Energy as a co-founding shareholder), part of Liu's capital contribution was his own non-patented wind-turbine gearbox design know-how, valued as intellectual-property capital.
notes: Highly relevant for an energy podcast (wind drivetrain supply chain). Low international media profile; route via company IR/board secretary office. Shares wealth listing with co-founder Kong Jinfeng.

name: Bo Shijiu
current_role: Founder, Executive Director & CEO, Changjiu Holdings (HKEX: 6959); Chairman, Beijing Changjiu Logistics (SSE: 603569)
profile: Automotive-logistics pioneer with 30+ years in the sector. He founded Changjiu Industrial in 1999 and has chaired Beijing Changjiu Logistics (car transport/supply-chain, Shanghai-listed 2016) since 2003; Changjiu Holdings, listed in Hong Kong in 2024, provides digital inventory-supervision services to auto dealers. Co-controls the group with his wife, chairwoman Li Guiping.
interesting_fact: He led Beijing Changjiu Logistics to a Shanghai Stock Exchange listing in August 2016 and later took a second business, Changjiu Holdings, public in Hong Kong in January 2024.
deep_cut_fact: His career began inside FAW: from 1993 to 2003 he headed First Automobile Works' Fada vehicle-delivery service department; he also earned a Jilin University business degree in 1997 while working and has been president of the CFLP China Automotive Logistics Association since 2010.
notes: Low international profile. Route via Changjiu Holdings / Beijing Changjiu Logistics IR (board secretary). Wealth shared with wife Li Guiping.

name: Liu Jianbo
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Kunshan Dongwei Technology Co. (东威科技, SSE STAR: 688700)
profile: Self-made engineer (b. 1979) who founded Dongwei in 2005; the company makes vertical continuous plating (VCP) equipment for PCB makers and has expanded into electroplating tools for semiconductors, photovoltaics and composite copper current-collector films for batteries. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; he holds roughly a third of the shares.
interesting_fact: Dongwei's VCP lines displaced traditional gantry-style plating in PCB plants, and the company has pushed the same technology into new-energy uses such as PV cell metallization and composite copper foil for lithium batteries.
deep_cut_fact: With a technical secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education, he started at about 17 as a technician at Dongguan Youda PCB equipment factory (1996-2001), then ran a small Kunshan machinery service shop (2001-05) before founding Dongwei.
notes: Energy-relevant (PV/battery plating equipment). Company holds regular online earnings Q&A sessions; IR email is the published channel.

name: He Boquan
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Today Investment (今日投资) - angel investor
profile: Guangdong entrepreneur who founded dairy-drink brand Robust (乐百氏) in 1989 and built the Today Group (今日集团, the 'Nowaday' in the listing), selling it to Danone and leaving with his founding team in 2001. After studying and travelling abroad, he set up Today Investment in 2003 and became one of China's best-known consumer-sector angel investors.
interesting_fact: He was the angel investor in budget hotel chain 7 Days in October 2004, holding about 37 million shares before its 2009 NYSE IPO.
deep_cut_fact: As an angel he says he almost never reads business plans, judging founders through a short conversation instead; reflecting on Robust he said 'giving up is sometimes harder than persisting, and more important' (放弃有时候比坚持还要难，而且还要重要).
notes: Input name_chinese (刘宪) does not match; correct name is 何伯权. 'Nowaday' = 今日 (Today) Group/Today Investment. Low-profile investor; no published direct contact found. Recent (2020s) activity not well documented.

name: David Rowland
current_role: Financier/investor; patriarch of the Rowland family investment group (Blackfish Capital), founder-owner of Banque Havilland (now Rangecourt S.A., winding down)
profile: British property developer and financier (b. 1945, nicknamed 'Spotty') who made early money in London property in the 1960s, then invested across shipping, timber and resources. In 2009 he and son Jonathan bought the 'good bank' carved out of Kaupthing Luxembourg, renamed Banque Havilland; the family also backed UK lender Redwood Bank. Based in Guernsey.
interesting_fact: He was the Conservative Party's largest donor in the run-up to the 2010 UK general election, giving about £2.8m after resuming full UK residency.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a scrap-metal dealer, he set up Fordham Investment Group in 1965 at about 20 and sold his stake in 1970 for £2.4m before moving to France at 24.
notes: Caution: heavy regulatory baggage - FCA/Upper Tribunal (Feb 2026) upheld findings against Banque Havilland over a plan to harm Qatar's economy; bank lost Luxembourg licence and has been renamed/sold off. Reputationally risky guest. No published direct contact; very private.

name: Zheng Chunying
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanghai Chando Group (自然堂集团, formerly Jala/伽蓝集团)
profile: Founder of Jala Group (renamed Chando Group), the Shanghai cosmetics company behind Chando (自然堂), Maysu, Chunxia, Ppureyen and baby-care brand Jichu. Chando launched in 2001 and has ranked first or second among domestic Chinese beauty brands by retail sales; the group, China's No.3 domestic cosmetics group in 2024, filed for a Hong Kong IPO in 2025.
interesting_fact: Chando markets itself as 'natural high-tech' sourced from the Himalayas and works with aerospace medicine: in Nov 2026 the group published research in the journal Space Medicine & Medical Engineering on applying space-medicine findings to skincare.
notes: Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so founder biography is thin; Chando's 2025 HKEX IPO prospectus would have a full director bio. Route via group media email.

name: Zheng Xiaodan
current_role: Vice Chairman, Beijing Yuanliu Hongyuan Electronic Technology Co. (鸿远电子, SSE: 603267); executive director of Hongyuan Suzhou
profile: Co-controlling shareholder (with her father, chairman Zheng Hong) of Hongyuan Electronics, a Beijing maker of high-reliability ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), filters, ICs, microwave modules and ceramic packages used largely in aerospace/defense electronics, plus a component-distribution arm. She rose through the company's marketing centre to vice chairman.
interesting_fact: She and her father are the company's joint actual controllers; Hongyuan's core high-reliability ceramic capacitor line (multilayer, single-layer, leaded and bracket types) saw a strong demand rebound in 2025, lifting output and margins.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family company she was a project manager at Beijing Zhongbiao Fangyuan, an anti-counterfeiting technology firm; she later earned an EMBA from Beihang University (Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics).
notes: Defense-electronics supplier; low media profile. Route via board secretary / IR email. Wealth shared with Zheng Hong.

name: He Ning
current_role: Chairman (and from 2019 general manager) of Beijing Honggao Creative Building Design Co. (弘高创意, ex-SZSE: 002504, since delisted); founder of Honggao decoration/design group
profile: Beijing entrepreneur (b. 1963) who built the Honggao interior-decoration and building-design group from 1993. In 2014 Honggao reverse-merged into Shenzhen-listed Dongguang Microelectronics, renamed Honggao Creative, with He Ning and Zhen Jiantao as actual controllers. The listed company later fell into delisting-risk status (2023) and has been delisted.
interesting_fact: Honggao went public via a 2014 reverse takeover of semiconductor firm Dongguang Microelectronics, which issued ~274m shares and handed control (about 60%) to Honggao's holding companies.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in finance from Tsinghua University's PBC School of Finance (Wudaokou) and is a senior engineer; he co-founded Honggao Decoration back in 1993.
notes: Listing name 'Zhen Jiatao' = 甄建涛 (filings), He Ning's co-controller. Last on Hurun 2017; listed company delisted after 2023 risk warning, so wealth likely much reduced. Web-search budget exhausted; current status unverified. Not a priority prospect.

name: Philipp Schindler
current_role: SVP & Chief Business Officer, Google / Alphabet Inc. (still filing Form 4s as an Alphabet insider as of Oct 2026)
profile: German executive (b. ~1971, Düsseldorf) who rose through Bertelsmann, CompuServe and AOL Germany before joining Google in Hamburg in 2005. He ran Northern & Central Europe, moved to Mountain View in 2012 to head global sales and operations, and since 2015 has been Chief Business Officer overseeing Google and YouTube sales, partnerships and customer support. His wealth comes from Alphabet stock.
interesting_fact: As CBO he oversaw roughly 29,000 people (about 17% of Google's workforce, as of 2022), making him one of the executives most responsible for Google's ad revenue engine.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Düsseldorf-Gerresheim, he was 'obsessed' with computers - his first was a Commodore 64 and he was writing software by 15; he was a Studienstiftung scholar and became AOL Germany's head of marketing & sales by 28. Off-duty he is into hydrofoiling, skiing and camping.
notes: Insider holdings confirmed via SEC EDGAR (CIK 0001837573). Not active on social media as far as found. Best route: Google press office or Google's AI/data-center business angle.

name: Yu Dehai
current_role: Co-actual controller of Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR: 688305) via Dalian Guangyang Science & Technology (光洋科技), its controlling shareholder
profile: Dalian industrialist behind Guangyang Science & Technology, the parent of Kede Numerical Control, one of China's leading makers of high-end five-axis CNC machine tools with in-house CNC systems, servo drives and motors. Kede listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; Yu Dehai and Yu Benhong are named together as controllers in its IPO commitments.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of the few Chinese companies to build both five-axis machining centres and their CNC control systems in-house, serving aerospace and power-generation turbine-blade machining, a field long dominated by Swiss/German suppliers.
notes: Very low public profile; Yu Benhong is Kede's chairman and day-to-day face. Web-search budget ran out, so Yu Dehai's personal bio and current status were not verified. Route via Kede board secretary/IR email.

name: Cheng Licai
current_role: Chairman, Hubei Shanhe Construction Group (湖北山河建设集团) - per latest available source
profile: Hubei construction and real-estate entrepreneur (b. 1962, Tuanfeng County) who chairs Shanhe Construction Group, a Wuhan-area contractor and property developer. A Communist Party member, he served as a Hubei deputy to the 11th and 12th National People's Congress. Appeared on the Hurun China list in 2021.
interesting_fact: He has served two terms as a deputy to China's National People's Congress for Hubei (from 2008 and 2013).
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tuanfeng County, Hubei, he trained as a construction engineer at Huazhong University of Science and Technology before building Shanhe into a regional construction group.
notes: Sparse public info (Wikipedia stub with dead references); web-search budget exhausted, so current role/status not re-verified. No published contact found; route would be via Shanhe Group's corporate office.

name: Chen Qingyuan
current_role: Co-founder, Yinlu Group (银鹭, Xiamen); current role not verified
profile: Co-founder of Xiamen food and drinks maker Yinlu, best known for canned eight-treasure porridge (八宝粥) and peanut milk. He and his brother Chen Qingshui started the business with four other young villagers in 1985; Nestlé bought 60% for RMB1.5bn in 2011 and later took full ownership, before selling the porridge and peanut-milk business back to the Chen Qingshui family's vehicle in 2020.
interesting_fact: Yinlu became one of Nestlé's biggest China acquisitions (60% for RMB1.5bn in 2011), and the founding family bought the core porridge and peanut-milk business back from Nestlé in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Yinlu started in 1985 as the Tong'an County Xinxu Xinghua Can Factory, founded by six young people from Majia Village in Xiamen, including Chen Qingyuan and his brother.
notes: Last on Hurun 2006-2009; brother Chen Qingshui is the better-known face of Yinlu. Web-search budget exhausted, so current role/status unverified. No published direct contact.

name: Simon Fuller
profile: British entertainment entrepreneur (b. 1960) who founded 19 Entertainment in 1985, managed the Spice Girls, Annie Lennox and David Beckham, and created the Idols format (Pop Idol, American Idol). He sold 19 to CKX in 2005 for $200m+ and launched XIX Entertainment in 2010, behind global pop group Now United; he also partners with Day One Music, whose artist Lola Young hit UK No. 1 in 2025.
interesting_fact: Billboard certified him in 2008 as the most successful British music manager of all time, and he has a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame (2011) - largely thanks to creating American Idol.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, in 1981, was at Chrysalis Music, where he signed Madonna's first hit 'Holiday' to the company; he grew up partly in Ghana, where his father was a headmaster, and attended school in Hastings.
notes: Social accounts are XIX company accounts, not personal. Best route: XIX Entertainment general inbox. Avoid personal-life topics (2025 divorce filing reported).

name: Lin Guofang
current_role: Chairman & General Manager (controlling shareholder), Shenzhen Fuanna Bedding & Furnishing Co. (富安娜, SZSE: 002327)
profile: Shenzhen home-textile entrepreneur (b. 1954, high-school education) who ran Shenzhen Yahao home-decor before founding Fuanna's predecessor in 1994. Fuanna grew into one of China's leading premium bedding and home-textile brands and listed in Shenzhen in 2009; he remains chairman, GM and actual controller per the 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: He personally funded about RMB200m to build the Lufeng city cultural centre plus a township hospital and middle school in Tanxi, Lufeng, earning the 'New Rural Worthy of South Guangdong' (南粤新乡贤) honour in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fuanna he was general manager of Shenzhen Yahao Home Décor (深圳雅豪家饰精品); he founded Fuanna in 1994 as 'Shenzhen Fuanna Home Decoration & Health Products Co.' and has run it for over 30 years.
notes: Hometown philanthropy in Lufeng (Shanwei, Guangdong) is a good warm angle. Route via Fuanna board office email.
